XOR '26 
ICT Competition Day of the Computer Society of Nalanda College 
Competition Guidelines 
General Information 
• Competition dates, registration deadlines, and submission deadlines will be announced. 
Registration and submission links will be provided separately. 
• Students may participate in multiple competitions. 
• Schools may enter any number of students in individual events, with one entry per 
participant per event. 
• Submitted files and links must remain accessible to the judges throughout the judging 
period. 
• No changes may be made to submitted work after the announced submission 
deadline. This includes hosted websites, repositories, design files, and Google Drive files. 
• Incomplete submissions, including entries missing required files or links, will be 
disqualified. 
• Participants must credit external resources used and follow the rules of their respective 
competition. 
1. Hackathon - Group Event 
Eligibility: Students in Grades 6-13. Each school may enter one team of up to four members. 
Themes 
Develop a technology-based solution under one of the following themes: 
• GreenTech - Technology for Nature: Environmental protection, conservation, or 
sustainable living. 
• EduTech - Rethinking Learning: Accessible education, interactive learning, or skill 
development. 
• CommunityTech - Connected Communities: Accessibility, transport, disaster 
preparedness, or local services. 
Preliminary Round - Online 
• Submit a project document in PDF format and a 3-5-minute video through Google 
Drive, with viewing access enabled for the judges. 
• Explain the problem, proposed solution, intended users, technologies used, and 
development progress. 
• Early-stage prototypes are accepted. Include a demonstration of the prototype and 
clearly identify features still under development. 
• Four teams will advance to the final. 
Final Round - On Site 
• Finalists must present a working prototype of their solution. 
• Selected teams may develop their projects further before the final. Any final submission 
deadline will be communicated to them. 
• The final begins at 2:00 p.m. on ICT Day. 
• Each team receives 10 minutes to present and demonstrate its project, followed by a 
question-and-answer session with the judges. 
Judging Criteria 
• Problem relevance and potential impact - 25% 
• Innovation and originality - 25% 
• Technical approach and feasibility - 20% 
• Implementation progress and demonstration - 20% 
• Presentation and understanding of the project - 10% 
2. ICT Quiz - Group Event 
Eligibility: Students in Grades 6-13. Each school may enter one team of four members. 
Competition Structure 
• Entry Round - Online: The top five teams advance to the Qualifier Round. 
• Qualifier Round - Online: The top two teams advance to the Final Round. 
• Final Round - On Stage: The two finalists compete live on ICT Day, following the 
hackathon final. 
Questions will cover general knowledge, the local O/L and A/L ICT syllabuses, logical 
thinking, problem-solving skills, and broader ICT knowledge. 
Round dates will be announced. Detailed guidelines, including the competition format, scoring 
system, and tie-breaking procedures, will be sent by email once a school registers. 
3. Web Development Challenge - Individual Event 
Eligibility: Students in Grades 6-13. 
Theme - Explore Responsibly 
Build a functional website for a fictional organization that helps people discover and protect Sri 
Lanka's natural attractions. 
Instructions 
• Include information about the organization, featured destinations, responsible travel 
practices, and a contact or inquiry section. 
• Include at least three pages or clearly defined sections. 
• Implement at least one working interactive feature, such as destination filtering, search, 
or a trip planner. 
• The website must work on desktop and mobile screens, with clear navigation and readable 
content. 
• The required interactive feature must be fully functional. Clearly labelled demonstration-only 
features will not count toward this requirement. 
• Any web technology may be used. External libraries are permitted with attribution, but 
copied websites and pre-made website templates are not allowed. 
• AI-generated code, content, and visuals, and AI-assisted development are not 
permitted. 
Submission 
Submit the hosted website link on any domain or hosting subdomain and the GitHub 
repository link. Both must be accessible to the judges. 
The repository must include the source files, asset credits, and any necessary setup instructions. 
Judging Criteria 
Functionality, usability and accessibility, responsive design, code quality, creativity, and relevance 
to the theme. 
4. UI/UX Design Challenge - Individual Event 
Eligibility: Students in Grades 6-13. 
Theme - Something Went Wrong: Upload Interrupted 
Design a mobile or web interface that helps a student recover when their internet connection drops 
while uploading a competition entry near the deadline. 
Instructions 
• Participants may use any recognized UI/UX design tool. 
• Include at least one primary interface screen, such as the submission page or 
dashboard. 
• Provide a short user flow or wireframe with at least three connected screens or states, 
showing the upload, interruption, and recovery. 
• Create a clickable prototype demonstrating the recovery journey. 
• Clearly communicate upload progress, what has been saved, available next steps, and the 
final submission status. 
• Include an alternative outcome where recovery fails or time runs out. 
• Designs must be original. Plagiarism and pre-made templates are not permitted. 
• The interface should demonstrate visual consistency, accessibility, and an understanding of 
the user's needs. 
• No coding or video submission is required. 
Scenario rule: An upload started before the deadline has a 10-minute grace period to complete 
submission. Afterward, the student may request organizer review without guaranteed acceptance. 
This rule applies only to the design scenario, not to this competition's actual submission deadline. 
Submission 
Submit: 
• The design file or accessible design link 
• An accessible clickable prototype link 
• The user flow or wireframes 
• A short explanation of the design decisions 
Judging Criteria 
• Recovery flow and problem-solving - 30% 
• Clarity of messages and next steps - 25% 
• Usability and accessibility - 20% 
• Visual hierarchy and consistency - 15% 
• Creativity and attention to detail - 10% 
5. Image Manipulation Challenge - Individual Event 
Eligibility: Students in Grades 6-13. 
Theme - Technology Meets Nature 
Create an original scene combining technology and nature through image manipulation. Explore 
how technological elements and natural environments can coexist. 
Instructions 
• Any image-editing software may be used. 
• The artwork must combine and manipulate source images into a cohesive composition. 
• AI tools and AI-generated images are not permitted. 
• Source images must be owned by the participant or permitted for reuse, with credits 
provided where applicable. 
Submission 
Submit a Google Drive folder link containing: 
• The final image in JPG or PNG format 
• The editable project file, such as PSD or the equivalent native format 
• All source images used in the artwork 
Enable viewing and downloading access for the judges. 
Judging Criteria 
Creativity, relevance to the theme, composition, quality of blending and manipulation, and attention 
to detail. 
The Web Development, UI/UX Design, and Image Manipulation challenges will be submitted 
and judged entirely online.
